title: RBI: Amendment — Reserve Bank of India (Urban Co-operative Banks – Know Your Customer) Amendment Directions, 2026
applicability: Urban Co-operative Banks dealing with Foreign Portfolio Investors (FPIs)
description: RBI has issued a amendment concerning Reserve Bank of India (Urban Co-operative Banks – Know Your Customer) Amendment Directions, 2026.
summary: The Reserve Bank of India issued the Reserve Bank of India (Urban Co-operative Banks – Know Your Customer) Amendment Directions, 2026, which modifies paragraph 4(1)(v) of the prior 2025 directions. The regulator took this action after reviewing extant instructions to extend certain document certification facilities. In practice, compliance workflows will now allow banks to alternatively accept original certified copies for Foreign Portfolio Investors (FPIs) authenticated by specified overseas authorities, matching the existing provisions for NRIs and PIOs.
takeaway: Update the bank's KYC verification procedures and documentation checklists to permit Foreign Portfolio Investors (FPIs) to submit original certified copies verified by the authorized overseas authorities, branches, or embassies specified in paragraph 4(1)(v).

takeaway: Provided that in case of Non-Resident Indians (NRIs) and Persons of Indian Origin (PIOs), as defined in Foreign Exchange Management (Deposit) Regulations, 2016 {FEMA 5(R)}, and Foreign Portfolio Investors (FPIs), the bank may alternatively obtain the original certified copy, certified by any one of the following: (a) authorised officials of overseas branches of Scheduled Commercial Banks registered in India, (b) branches of overseas banks with whom Indian banks have relationships, (c) Notary Public abroad, (d) Court Magistrate, (e) Judge, (f) Indian Embassy / Consulate General in the country where the non-resident customer resides.
effective_date: These Directions shall come into force with immediate effect.

title: RBI: Notification — Reserve Bank of India (Small Finance Banks – Know Your Customer) Amendment Directions, 2026
description: RBI has issued a notification concerning Reserve Bank of India (Small Finance Banks – Know Your Customer) Amendment Directions, 2026.
summary: The Reserve Bank of India has amended paragraph 5(1)(v) of the Small Finance Banks – Know Your Customer Directions, 2025. This change was made to extend an existing facility to Foreign Portfolio Investors (FPIs) after a review of extant instructions. In practice, compliance workflows for onboarding FPIs will now permit banks to alternatively obtain original certified copies certified by specified overseas authorities, branches, or officials.
takeaway: Update the KYC verification and onboarding procedures for Foreign Portfolio Investors (FPIs) to accept original certified copies certified by the permitted overseas authorities, branches, or officials listed in paragraph 4(1) of the Amendment Directions.

title: IBBI: Circular — Extension of time for filing Forms to monitor insolvency resolution processes for Personal Guarantors to Corporate Debtors
applicability: All Registered Insolvency Professionals, All Recognised Insolvency Professional Entities, and All Registered Insolvency Professional Agencies
description: IBBI has issued a circular concerning Extension of time for filing Forms to monitor insolvency resolution processes for Personal Guarantors to Corporate Debtors.
summary: The Board has extended the last date for submission of all applicable PGIRP forms (PGIRP-1 to PGIRP-6) to monitor the insolvency resolution processes for personal guarantors to corporate debtors until 30th September 2026. This extension was granted in response to representations from Insolvency Professionals and Insolvency Professional Agencies citing technicalities, difficulties, and the transitional time required to familiarize themselves with the electronic platform. In practice, compliance workflows now allow submissions and penalty-free modifications up to the new September deadline, while requiring insolvency professionals to ensure all submitted information is accurate and fully consistent with supporting documents.
takeaway: Review the official document and ensure all applicable PGIRP forms are submitted accurately and truthfully by 30th September 2026 to avoid penalties.

description: Insolvency and Bankruptcy Board of India

Subject: Extension of time for filing Forms to monitor insolvency resolution processes for 
Personal Guarantors to Corporate Debtors under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 
2016, and the regulations made thereunder.
summary:
The last date for submission of all applicable PGIRP forms as per paragraph 9 of 
Circular No. IBBI/II/92/2026 is hereby extended till 30th September 2026.

In this regard, representations have been received from Insolvency Professionals (IPs) 
and Insolvency Professional Agencies (IPAs) requesting an extension of the deadline, 
citing technicalities, difficulties, and the transitional time required to familiarize 
themselves with the electronic platform and submission of the forms.

In this regard, it is 
strictly directed that IPs shall ensure all information submitted via the PGIRP forms is 
accurate, truthful, and entirely consistent with the supporting documents attached 
thereto.
takeaway:
The last date for submission of all applicable PGIRP forms as per paragraph 9 of 
Circular No. IBBI/II/92/2026 is hereby extended till 30th September 2026.

In line with this extension, penalties for delayed submission or modification of these 
forms shall now be levied only after 30th September 2026.
